name: Hazelnut
description: Hazelnut (Corylus avellana) represents the seed of a deciduous shrub, functioning as a high-energy botanical matrix packed with monounsaturated lipids, specific amino acid profiles, and robust mineral clusters. Structurally, the kernel is an dense array of oleic acid triglycerides shielded by a fibrous skin rich in proanthocyanidin polyphenols. This superfood operates as a potent neuroprotective and metabolic modulator, leveraging its lipid-soluble antioxidant capacity to preserve vascular endothelial integrity and drive skeletal matrix cross-linking, while providing sustained fuel for cognitive energy requirements.
macroIntro: The macronutrient profile is characterized by a high thermodynamic density dominated by oleic-rich lipids, structural plant proteins, and a slow-release carbohydrate-fiber matrix.
microIntro: A critically dense reservoir of trace minerals and fat-soluble antioxidants essential for neutralizing intracellular oxidative cascades.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Significant caloric payload originating from the complete beta-oxidation of long-chain fatty acids.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: A valuable plant-based amino acid profile rich in L-arginine, a critical precursor for endothelial nitric oxide production.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Lipid fraction dominated by monounsaturated oleic acid, which maintains cell membrane fluidity and cardiovascular homeostasis.

macroNutrients.name: Total Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: A complex botanical saccharide array providing steady-state glucose substrates alongside high-density insoluble structural fibers.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: A sophisticated structural cellulose and lignin matrix that regulates mechanical gastrointestinal transit and postprandial insulinemia.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin E (Tocopherol)
microNutrients.description: A primary lipid-soluble antioxidant that protects cellular phospholipid bilayers from lipid peroxidation.

microNutrients.name: Manganese
microNutrients.description: A critical enzymatic cofactor for superoxide dismutase, directly neutralizing reactive mitochondrial oxygen species.

microNutrients.name: Copper
microNutrients.description: An essential transition metal cofactor for lysyl oxidase, which facilitates cross-linking of structural collagen and elastin proteins.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: A fundamental intracellular cation modulating nerve transmission, muscle relaxation, and stabilized adenosine triphosphate synthesis.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)
microNutrients.description: A coenzyme driving the decarboxylation of alpha-keto acids, facilitating rapid energy metabolism within the central nervous system.

healthBenefits: Neuroprotective and Cognitive Enhancement: High-dose tocopherols and thiamine synergistically protect neuronal mitochondrial membranes, facilitating superior signal transduction and long-term synaptic integrity.
Cardiovascular Lipid Homeostasis: Oleic acid and structural fibers act in concert to decrease low-density lipoprotein (LDL) oxidation, preserving arterial lumen elasticity.
Endogenous Antioxidant Supercharging: The massive manganese content activates intracellular superoxide dismutase (SOD) systems, providing a systemic defense against chronic oxidative degradation.
Skeletal and Connective Tissue Matrix Support: High concentrations of copper and magnesium enable the robust cross-linking of bone proteins and cartilage fibers, reinforcing structural rigidity.
precautionsIntro: The high caloric and lipid density requires precise nutritional integration, alongside the management of potential anti-nutritional and biological variables:
precautions: Severe Allergic Reactivity: The kernel contains potent tree nut proteins capable of triggering life-threatening anaphylactic responses in sensitized phenotypes.

Phytic Acid Mineral Sequestration: High concentrations of phytic acid in the raw state may reduce the bio-availability of divalent cations like iron and zinc, a risk mitigated by thermal processing or soaking.

Aflatoxin and Fungal Proliferation: Improper moisture management during storage creates a high-risk matrix for Aspergillus flavus colonization and subsequent secondary mycotoxin (aflatoxin) accumulation.
